description: A cosine oscillator whose phase is bent towards a pulse or a saw, with that bent phase brought out for driving other oscillators

params.text: Sets the pitch, -14 to 4 as a power of two around middle C, which is about 0.016Hz to 4186Hz
Sets where the middle of the cycle falls, 0 to 1; away from the centre the wave leans towards a saw
Sets how much of each half of the cycle is flattened at its ends, 0 to 1, which squares the wave off towards a pulse
Attenuates the voltage at the Skew jack before it is added to the Skew knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Clip jack before it is added to the Clip knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Scales the voltage at the FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the FM jack is added to the frequency in hertz rather than to the pitch in octaves, which gives through-zero frequency modulation

inputs.text: Sets the pitch by cable, 1V per octave added to the knob, one channel per voice
Drives the wave from an outside phase over -5V to 5V; while a cable is patched here the pitch knob and the V/Oct jack are passed over
Modulates the skew, a tenth per volt scaled by the knob below it
Modulates the clipping, a tenth per volt scaled by the knob below it
Modulates the frequency through the FM knob; with Lin off it is added to the pitch in octaves, and with Lin on it is added to the frequency itself, which lets it pass through zero

outputs.text: The bent phase as a rising ramp over -5V to 5V, for driving a phase driven oscillator
The cosine of the bent phase, -5V to 5V

notes: used as an FM operator, the modulation is carried in the bent phase as well, so an oscillator driven from the Phs output is modulated through it
menu: Oversample — runs the oscillator sixteen times over per sample and filters the result, which cuts the aliasing of the harder settings; it is passed over while a cable is in the Phs input
